It exists in iris-sast/zip4j, which is NOT a mirror or fork (fork=false, parent=null, created 2025-06-30) but a synthetic benchmark repo built from decompiled sources JARs — 59aeea59 is a 2025-07-09 commit titled 'Add decompiled source for 1.3.3 (fixed) from zip4j-1.3.3-sources.jar', child of the 1.3.2 'vulnerable' commit. So our official_fix.patch content is genuine 1.3.3 code; only the SHA is synthetic, and the dataset's github_url for this row points at that reconstructed repo. RE-INTRODUCTION CLAIM CORRECTED: we credited c158768 (2019-09-05, '#55 ZipSlip fix') with re-introducing the boundary-less check in 2.x. Refuted — c158768 only canonicalized the LEFT operand. That makes the recurrence thesis stronger, not weaker: the same defect was written into the rewrite the day after it was fixed in the old line.

jeremylong__DependencyCheck_CVE-2018-120.notes: COUNT CONFIRMED, REACHABILITY OVERSTATED — severity must come down before any disclosure. The 6 boundary-less sites at HEAD (02bb473c, 2026-08-18) are confirmed at lines 103/116 (extractFiles(File,File,Engine)), 170/179 (extractFiles(InputStream,File)), 246 (private extractArchive) and 286 (private extractFile), and they are the only startsWith occurrences in the file. But a grep of the whole HEAD tree for ExtractionUtil callers shows: (a) the overload THIS PoV drives, extractFiles(File,File[,Engine]), has ZERO production callers — only its own unit test; it is public library API of dependency-check-core, reachable only by a third-party embedder; (b) extractFiles(InputStream,File) has one caller, AssemblyAnalyzer.extractGrokAssembly, on a resource inside dependency-check's own JAR — not attacker-controlled; (c) sites 246/286 are reached from PythonDistributionAnalyzer, which is @Experimental and OFF BY DEFAULT (analyzer.experimental.enabled=false), and its file branch runs only behind NameFileFilter('METADATA'/'PKG-INFO'). SEVERITY CEILING we had been missing: a boundary-less startsWith admits only paths whose canonical form has the destination's FULL path string as a prefix, and both reachable destinations are program-chosen random temp dirs (<temp>/check<random>tmp/<N>), so the escape reaches only siblings inside dependency-check's own scratch tree — it cannot reach /etc, ~/.ssh, or the scanned project. NOT arbitrary file write. Drop 'zip slip'/'arbitrary write' framing; expect a triager to rate this low/informational. NOTE a conflict between two audits: one recommended leading the report with archiveanalyzer_sibling_prefix as the default-reachable half, but the other established (tag-by-tag counts + git log -S) that the ArchiveInputStream overload that PoV drives has been safe since v5.0.0-M1 in 2019; the two guards still unsafe in ArchiveAnalyzer at HEAD (467/482) are the gz/bz2 branches, whose output name derives from the archive's own filename, and no PoV of ours drives them. So neither PoV is a default-reachable arbitrary-write finding.

jeremylong__DependencyCheck_CVE-2018-120.reachability_notes: BOTH prior claims re-confirmed by a second audit, including a GitHub-wide code search. ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS: extractFiles(File,File) is called only by its own unit test, and a search for external embedders calling it on untrusted input returned only forks, mirrors and dataset copies. The two paths that DO process untrusted archives are siblings, not this overload: extractFiles(InputStream,File) extracts a JAR resource bundled inside dependency-check itself, and extractFilesUsingFilter is reached only from PythonDistributionAnalyzer, which is @Experimental and off by default. CONFINEMENT: every reachable destination is a program-chosen random temp dir, so the boundary-less startsWith admits only paths textually prefixed by that temp path — an escape lands in a sibling inside dependency-check's own scratch tree, never /etc, ~/.ssh or the scanned project. NOT arbitrary file write. Drop all zip-slip framing; a triager would rate this low/informational.

perwendel__spark_CVE-2016-9177_2.5.1::sh.notes: Confirmed at master HEAD (1973e402, 2022-07-10): isPathWithinFolder is still a bare String.startsWith with no separator boundary. Chain re-verified at HEAD: ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource -> protectAgainstInClassPath(resource.getPath(), baseResource), and ClassPathResource's constructor does StringUtils.cleanPath (converts backslashes, collapses ..) and strips the leading slash, so '/..\\publicSECRET/x' arrives as 'publicSECRET/x' against folder 'public' and startsWith returns true. Signature changed since 2.5.1 — the folder is now a parameter, not StaticFilesFolder.local(); cite the HEAD signature. removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom, added after the CVE fix, makes it slightly WORSE: it trims a trailing slash, so even a base configured as 'public/' is reduced to 'public' before the prefix test. MAINTENANCE REALITY for disclosure planning: not archived but effectively unmaintained — last master commit 2022-07-10, latest tag 2.9.3 (2020-10-08), ZERO GitHub releases ever published, 262 open issues / 56 open PRs, 9.6k stars. Treat as a no-response disclosure target.
perwendel__spark_CVE-2016-9177_2.5.1::sh.reachability_notes: The public HTTP static chain is real (StaticFilesConfiguration.consume:67 -> consumeWithFileResourceHandlers:91 -> getResource(servletPath+pathInfo) -> ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource:83) and the boundary bug is real at HEAD (DirectoryTraversal.java:30-34, bare startsWith). But exploitation needs a sibling CLASSPATH resource directory whose name shares the static folder's prefix (publicSECRET next to public) AND containing a secret the developer did not mean to serve — a layout that does not occur in a normal staticFiles.location('/public') app — and it relies on backslash/'..' surviving container URI normalisation into getPathInfo(). Preconditions unrealistic. DISPOSITION: harden startsWith to a separator boundary; not an advisory.

perwendel__spark_CVE-2016-9177_2.5.1::sy.notes: Confirmed at HEAD: unixifyPath uses Paths.get(path).toAbsolutePath(), which performs no symlink resolution (that needs toRealPath()), and the input is ExternalResource.getPath() — the literal path. WORDING CORRECTION: we call this an 'adjacent weakness', which is defensible on root cause (missing canonicalization vs ../ traversal), but the defect lives INSIDE the guard method the CVE fix introduced, so a triager will read it as a second bypass of the same guard. Say 'distinct root cause in the same guard', not 'unrelated weakness'.
perwendel__spark_CVE-2016-9177_2.5.1::sy.reachability_notes: The defect is real — protectAgainstForExternal checks the literal resource.getPath(), not getCanonicalPath(), so a symlink under the served base is followed (ExternalResourceHandler.getResource:82). But the attacker must PLANT a symlink inside the served external directory, i.e. hold local filesystem write to the web root — and anyone with that can already do worse. Not a remote vulnerability. Defense-in-depth only.
